rule: `self.m()` / `this.m()` / a bare call to a member of the enclosing type → `Type#m`. If `m` is defined only on a superclass that is in the scan, the callee is `Superclass#m`. | Call on a **computed receiver** (call result, index, literal, `super` when the superclass is not in the scan): `.member` — a leading dot means "receiver unknown". | **medium**: the callee is named statically (Type.m(), module.f(), an import, `self.m()` inherited from a base outside the scan, an external library type) but is not defined in the scan.
notes: call_type convention used throughout this corpus: a callee that is a member of a type (`T#m`) or a receiver-qualified guess (`recv.m`, `.m`) is `method`; a C function (bare name) is `direct`. `baseWork` is defined only on the scanned superclass → `Base#baseWork`. `super` is a computed receiver only when the superclass is not in the scan; here Base is scanned and defines baseWork → `Base#baseWork` high. `description` is defined by neither scanned class; it is inherited from NSObject outside the scan → enclosing type `Derived#description`, medium (tier rule; C2 'inherited from a base outside the scan').
